Example: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule
?

EXPLANATION

Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:
steps.name: Example: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

worked_solution.markdown:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:


$\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int {x}^{0}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{2+1}}{2+1})+x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x+C\end{aligned}$

worked_solution.html: Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get
worked_solution.markdown:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{3}-x\,\text{d}x & =2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x-\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(\frac{{x}^{3+1}}{3+1})-(\frac{{x}^{1+1}}{1+1})+C \\  & =2(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})-(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

steps.name: Example: Integrating Sums of Power Functions

worked_solution.html: Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get
worked_solution.markdown:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5(\sqrt{x}{)}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+5)\,\text{d}x & =\int (5{x}^{3/2}-4{x}^{2}+5)\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int {x}^{3/2}\,\text{d}x-4\int {x}^{2}\text{d}x+5\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(\frac{{x}^{5/2}}{\frac{5}{2}})-4(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})+5(x)+C \\  & =5\cdot \frac{2}{5}{x}^{5/2}-\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}+5x+C \\  & =2\sqrt{{x}^{5}}-\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}+5x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

∫4−1y5/2dy=4∫1dy−∫y−5/2dy=4∫y0dy−∫y−5/2dy=4(y0+10+1)−(y−5/2+1−52+1)+C=4y−(y−3/2−32)+C=4y+23y3/2+C
worked_solution.markdown:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4-\frac{1}{{y}^{5/2}}\,\text{d}y & =4\int 1\,\text{d}y-\int {y}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4\int {y}^{0}\,\text{d}y-\int {y}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4(\frac{{y}^{0+1}}{0+1})-(\frac{{y}^{-5/2+1}}{-\frac{5}{2}+1})+C \\  & =4y-(\frac{{y}^{-3/2}}{-\frac{3}{2}})+C \\  & =4y+\frac{2}{3{y}^{3/2}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

worked_solution.markdown:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-3x\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{-2}-3x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x-3\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(-{x}^{-1})-3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+C \\  & =-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{x}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

prompt.html: Find the antiderivative of 5x+2x3.

worked_solution.html:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

∫5x+2x3dx=∫5xdx+∫2x3dx=5∫xdx+2∫x3dx=5(x22)+2(x44)+C=x42+5x22+C.
worked_solution.markdown:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int 5x+2{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & =\int 5x\,\text{d}x+\int 2{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int x\,\text{d}x+2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+2(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+\frac{5{x}^{2}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(3-{x}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (9-6{x}^{2}+{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{4}\,\text{d}x-6\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+9\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}-6(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})+9x+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}-2{x}^{3}+9x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

∫(1+x2)2dx=∫(1+2x2+x4)dx=∫x4dx+2∫x2dx+∫1dx=(x55)+2(x33)+(x)+C=x55+2x33+x+C.
worked_solution.markdown:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1+{x}^{2}{)}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (1+2{x}^{2}+{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+2\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})+2(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})+(x)+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}+x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

prompt.html: Find the antiderivative of x4−3x5+x65.

worked_solution.html:
